newsitem.title: USA: Producer prices rise 0.4 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: Producer prices rise 0.4 percent in October.

text.p: Prices at the wholesale level rose moderately in October, the Labor Department said Wednesday, with both food and energy prices moving higher as the slowing economy entered the fourth quarter.
The department said the Producer Price Index rose 0.4 percent, after being up 0.2 percent in September.
With the often-volatile food and energy sector excluded, the so-called core rate, however, fell 0.3 percent after being up the same amount in the prior month.
Wall Street had estimated the overall rate would rise 0.2 percent and the core would gain 0.1 percent.
The release of the new inflation data comes just shortly before the Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets to discuss the future course of interest rates.
Most analysts have taken the view that the Fed will stand pat, generally satisfied with the slowing pace of the overall economy and the level of inflation.
The department said that food prices rose 0.8 percent in October, compared with a 0.2 percent rise in September. The increase was fuelled by price rises for meat, fish and vegetables.
Energy prices jumped 1.9 percent after being up 0.2 percent in September, with gasoline rising 5.5 percent and heating oil up 3.8 percent.
Passenger car prices fell 1.6 percent in October after jumping 1.2 percent the prior month. Tobacco prices rose 0.3 percent.
Prices of intermediate goods -- those that require further processing -- were unchanged last month after increasing 0.3 percent in September.
The department said the rise in overall prices was largest since March, when they rose 0.5 percent, while the fall in the core rate was the largest since the 0.4 percent drop in October 94.
